change_summary: The journal retracted the article. An institutional investigation found the data in Figures 2 to 4 had been fabricated. The notice says the conclusions cannot be relied on. The paper's Figures 2 to 4 show n-back accuracy by dose, its main result.
evaluation: Your Introduction cites Brown and Kim [3] as showing that 200 mg of caffeine improves working memory by 12%, and says this is why you chose a 200 mg dose. The paper reports that 200 mg caffeine improved n-back accuracy by 12% compared with placebo, and says Figures 2 to 4 show accuracy by dose. The journal retracted the article, and the notice says the data in Figures 2 to 4 had been fabricated and the conclusions cannot be relied on. This touches the only place your draft cites the paper, and it is the basis for your dose choice, so the impact on your draft is high.
recommendation: The journal retracted the article, and the notice says the data in Figures 2 to 4 had been fabricated and the conclusions cannot be relied on. Your Introduction cites Brown and Kim [3] as showing that 200 mg of caffeine improves working memory by 12%, which is why you chose a 200 mg dose. Raise the dose choice with your co-authors or supervisor, since your experiment's design rests on this result and editing the text will not fix it. Then remove or replace the citation, find independent support for the dose, and re-check the claim it supported.
